### 1. Coordinates and circumcenter

Place
\[
B=(0,0),\qquad C=(14,0).
\]
If \(A=(x,y)\), then
\[
x^2+y^2=13^2,\qquad (x-14)^2+y^2=15^2.
\]
Subtracting gives \(x=5\), so take
\[
A=(5,12).
\]

The circumcenter lies on \(x=7\). Write \(O=(7,t)\). Equating \(OA^2=OB^2\),
\[
4+(12-t)^2=49+t^2,
\]
which gives
\[
t=\frac{33}{8}.
\]
Thus
\[
O=\left(7,\frac{33}{8}\right).
\]

### 2. Determine the rotation

We have
\[
\overrightarrow{AC}=(9,-12).
\]
The rotation matrix
\[
R=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac45&\frac35\\[2pt]
-\frac35&\frac45
\end{pmatrix}
\]
satisfies
\[
R(9,-12)=(0,-15),
\]
so it makes \(A'C'\) vertical, hence perpendicular to \(BC\). The other possible rotation is \(-R\), but it places \(A'\) and \(B\) on the same side of \(B'C'\), so it is excluded.

Using \(P'=O+R(P-O)\), we obtain
\[
A'=\left(\frac{81}{8},\frac{93}{8}\right),\qquad
C'=\left(\frac{81}{8},-\frac{27}{8}\right),\qquad
B'=\left(-\frac{43}{40},\frac{201}{40}\right).
\]

Indeed, line \(B'C'\) has equation
\[
3x+4y=\frac{135}{8}.

At \(A'\), \(3x+4y=\frac{615}{8}\), while at \(B\) it is \(0\), so \(A'\) and \(B\) are on opposite sides, as required.

### 3. Area of the hexagon

Apply the shoelace formula to
\[
A,\ A',\ C,\ C',\ B,\ B'.
\]
The two shoelace sums are
\[
S_1
=5\cdot\frac{93}{8}
+14\left(-\frac{27}{8}\right)
+\left(-\frac{43}{40}\right)(12)
=-\frac{81}{40},
\]
and
\[
S_2
=12\cdot\frac{81}{8}
+\frac{93}{8}\cdot14
+\frac{201}{40}\cdot5
=\frac{12375}{40}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
[\text{hexagon}]
=\frac12\left|S_1-S_2\right|
=\frac12\left|\frac{-81-12375}{40}\right|
=\frac{1557}{10}
=155.7.
